overview: Budget analysts help governments, universities and companies plan and control spending. They review department budget requests, track monthly spending reports, study trends and advise managers on costs and funding choices. O*NET rates their conventional interest at a maximum 7.00 and knowledge of economics and accounting at 4.42 out of 5. Most hold a bachelor's degree, 78% in O*NET data, often in accounting, finance or public finance. The BLS May 2025 median is $91,640 across 47,160 jobs. The work is quiet desk work with regular hours and tight deadlines at budget time.
pay: Budget analysts earn a median of $91,640, and the top 10% earn $136,660 or more. The District of Columbia has the highest state median at $124,590, 36% above the national figure, because many federal agencies are based there. Maryland and Virginia follow. California has the most jobs, 4,160.

faq.q: How much do budget analysts make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $91,640 a year. The middle half earn between $75,320 and $114,220. The District of Columbia, Maryland ($106,020) and Virginia ($105,470) have the highest state medians, while Kentucky ($76,860) and Arkansas ($71,800) pay the least.

faq.q: What degree do you need to be a budget analyst?
faq.a: Most budget analysts have a bachelor's degree, which 78% hold in O*NET data, while 8% have a master's degree. There are 4 related majors: accounting, accounting and finance, finance and public finance. Government jobs may value a master's degree in public administration.

faq.q: What skills do budget analysts need?
faq.a: O*NET rates critical thinking and mathematics at 3.88 out of 5 for this job. Knowledge of economics and accounting is rated 4.42. Spreadsheets matter, but so do speaking and active listening, rated 3.75, because you explain spending choices to managers.

faq.q: What can budget analysts move into?
faq.a: Treasurers and Controllers are a 94% match. Financial Managers are an 88% match and earn $166,570, 82% more, according to BLS May 2025 data. Compensation and Benefits Managers are an 86% match and earn $149,230, 63% more. All three build on budgeting experience.
